# Changelog

All notable changes to JAPES (JazzX SDK) will be documented in this file.

## [2.7.0] - unreleased

Plan: `docs/plans/plan_JAPES_2_7_0_EXPERT_SURFACE_AND_ANSWER_CONTRACT.md` (drift-checked), `docs/plans/plan_2_7_0_tenancy_hardening.md`. Entries land here as the work does.

- **The bundled Acra DSCR starter lists jobs (+2,260 / -6 lines, 6 files).** The seed policy pack (0.3.0, not bumped) gains `policies/jobs.yaml`: 37 procedure jobs in three policies (`DSCR_PROCESS_JOBS` core, `DSCR_STANDARD_JOBS` and `DSCR_PLATINUM_SELECT_JOBS` as the two programs' policies), one job per topic of the matching grid policy (loan amount, location, concessions, CLTV grid, minimum DSCR, reserves, credit score and history, property type, rental use, vacant, listing, condo, borrower status, first-time buyer, entity, critical validation, interest-only, escrow waiver, prepayment buyout, cash-out lease), each carrying the rules it covers as its checks and the case fields they read. The manifest lists the job policies under their programs and sets the assessment step to `engine_mode: code_only` (the jobs are listed, not run, so the deterministic assessment is unchanged). The seed blueprint `acra-dscr` is 0.3.0 (policy and assistant; the legacy `core` member, the pre-rename copy of the policy, is dropped). Limits of the source: the jobs restate the 106 existing rules, so they add no requirement the rules do not already hold; steps are the pack's four-step outline with topic wording, no per-job document list is declared (`evidence_types` is empty), the whole-pack job set export lists only the core process jobs (product-scope job policies are not exported without a program overlay declaration), and no reference job set or alignment ships. New `tests/test_seed_acra_jobs.py` asserts every program lists jobs, every grid rule is a check of one, and each read is declared by the pack template; two pack tests update their expected policy ids.

- **Recipes gap R2.4: an eval case is adjudicated the way a case run adjudicates it (`pipelines/steps.py`, `pack/eval_invoker.py`, `server/eval_wiring.py`, `tests/test_case_conditions.py`, `tests/test_adjudication_eval.py`; +164 / -43 lines, 5 files).** `AdjudicationInvoker` built one segment over every active live rule with a bare agent (only `model` and `replicas`), so an eval case could reach outcomes a case run on the same input would not. The case step's setup is now three shared functions in `pipelines/steps.py`, used by the step and the invoker alike: `adjudication_scope` (the rules the assessment leaves in force, each rule's policy and program), `live_rules_of` (the rules a model judges, and those left pending) and `adjudication_segments` (one segment per policy). For a pack whose case pipeline has an `adjudication` step the invoker now takes the pack's agent file (with `model` and `replicas` as overrides), runs the assessment first (so rules not in force are left out and the derived figures reach the context), segments by policy, uses the same collapse and subjects, applies each rule's default action and numbers conditions; it takes a `python_executor` (wired in `eval_wiring`). A pack with no such step keeps the old one-segment behavior. No behavior change to the case step (the 1022 tests over adjudication, eval, rule trials and the wiring pass). Tests: a case run and an eval case on the same input with a scripted model reach the same outcomes, statuses, actions and condition ids, with a not-yet-in-force policy left out of both; it fails on the old invoker (the action was not defaulted, and the future rule was judged). The eval test's pack stub now carries a loader, as a real pack does, and the file restores the environment its Plato app writes.

- **Catalog slice P6: checked, nothing new registered (scratch plan items 31 and 32).** `policy_change_to_impact`: the comparison of two pack versions exists (`pack/release_report.compare_packs`, `GET /packs/{id}/release-report`: jobs, rules, documents, catalog, coverage and the gold cases whose answers move, no model); what is missing is naming the open cases that need a rerun, which is recorded as a follow-up, and it is a report, not a runnable pipeline, so it is not in the pipeline registry. `feedback_to_improvements`: the parts exist (an approved correction becomes a gold case in `pack/correction_cases.py`; a correction is diagnosed to a layer with a ranked fix list in `pack/diagnosis.py`; eval signals become guidance proposals in `modes/evolve/curator.py`) but are not composed into one run; recorded as a follow-up with the knowledge-loop plan. P4 (`policy_to_code`, `policy_to_pack`) waits on the user's answers to the design note `note_policy_to_code_and_pack_design_2026-11-06`.

- **The formal compiler skips procedure jobs (`formal/compiler.py`, `tests/test_formal_canonical_policy.py`; +60 / -0 lines, 2 files).** `compile_canonical_policy` lowered every active rule, and a procedure rule raised "condition kind 'procedure' is not in the JSON comparison subset" and was recorded as a gap; with the Acra starter's 37 procedure jobs that made every program's check `CANNOT_DETERMINE` and failed two seed-program tests. A procedure is a job a model follows, not a formal subject, so the compiler now skips it (`engine_modes.is_procedure`, as the code-only assessment does). **A procedure job no longer appears as a gap**; a rule that really cannot be lowered still does. A selection that holds only procedure jobs now raises "the selection holds no canonical rules to compile" instead of compiling to a pack of gaps. Family check: the other consumers of the compiled pack's gaps (`json_rules`, the local formal request builder) read the compiled output, so they see only the change above; the 14 test files that touch the formal path pass (355). Tests fail on the old compiler: a pack with a job compiles to no rule and no gap for it and the same verdict as without it, an unlowerable prose rule beside a job is still the only gap, a jobs-only selection is refused with a clear message, and the two seed-program tests.

- **Open conditions of a case, catalog slice P5 completed (`pipelines/steps.py`, `pipelines/kinds.py`, `pipelines/catalog.py`, `agents/adjudication/conditions.py`, `tests/test_case_conditions.py`; +182 / -6 lines, 5 files).** New step kind `conditions` and slot `conditions`; `CaseState.conditions` and `CaseResult.conditions` hold one row per open adjudication condition (the `OutcomeCondition` fields, its `rule_id`, `source: rule`, and now the outcome's evidence `citations`, added to `open_condition_rows`, which the run output, the case-run ground source and the scorers share) followed by one row per required document class the case has none of (`kind: document`, `id: D-<class>`, `source: document`, `documents: [class]`; `timing` and `party` empty until `ClassNeed` carries them). Rule-condition ids are the adjudication's own (`C1`...) and stay stable across a rerun; the document ids are the class name. Preset `case_file_to_conditions`: documents, assessment, adjudication, conditions (no approval), with a registry entry; `case_update_to_verdicts` is not a preset: the `case_to_verdicts` entry now says a submit that names the run it follows is the update mode. Proved on a synthetic pack with a scripted model and one missing document (no shipped pack switched to adjudication, no billed run): the list, a case with nothing missing, ids unchanged on a rerun, and a new document clearing the missing one. Clearing is read-only in this slice: no route in `plato/api` sets a condition's `resolution` (the `resolution` in `runs.py` is the human checkpoint's), recorded as a follow-up.

- **A case preset: a pack names `case_to_verdicts` instead of listing its steps, catalog slice P5 in part (`pipelines/kinds.py`, `pipelines/catalog.py`, `tests/test_case_presets.py`; +152 / -2 lines, 3 files).** A `conductor_pipeline` block may carry `preset: case_to_verdicts` and a `steps` mapping of step id to that step's settings; the preset fixes the ids, kinds and order (documents `document_ingest`, assessment `policy_assessment`, investigation, approval `human_checkpoint`, narrative `narrate`), `step_entries` expands it, and the block is validated (unknown preset, a step the preset does not have, a list where a mapping belongs, a `kind` or `id` inside a step's settings). `ConductorPipelineConfig` gains `preset` and accepts a mapping for `steps`; a block with no preset still needs a list or a file. `case_to_verdicts` is also a registry entry (steps listed, no builder). Acceptance: the DSCR seed pack's hand-written step list, rewritten in preset form, expands to exactly the same entries, and a pack built from it has the same case plan (ids, kinds and every step's settings) and the same conductor problems. The seed pack itself is unchanged. Not built, and why: `case_update_to_verdicts` already exists as a submit option (a rerun names the run it follows, with `when_unchanged`), not as steps, so a step preset would not add it; `case_file_to_conditions` needs a conditions output and a completeness step that do not exist yet (the document step's `required_classes` is the completeness check today), which is design, not a preset. Both are put to the user.

- **Pipelines are named by input and output, catalog slices P2 and P3 (`pipelines/catalog.py`, `tests/test_pipeline_catalog.py`, `tests/test_vocabulary_pipeline.py`; +201 / -38 lines, 3 files).** Registry ids: `question_to_answer` (was `chat`), `documents_to_fields` (`document_ingest`), `documents_to_vocabulary` (`vocabulary_build`), `filings_to_spread` (`financial_spread`), `case_to_decision` (`investigation_loop`); the single `policy_extract` entry is now three, sharing the stages (`ingest` to `finalize`) and each fixing the run representation it serves (`representation`): `policy_to_rules` (`obligations`), `policy_to_jtbds` (`jtbd`), `jtbds_to_code` (`python_jobs`); `catalog_extract` and `documents_extract` join as `policy_to_catalog` and `policy_to_document_list` (declared stages read_parts, check_excerpts, join_names, classify, file_proposals; no builder, since they are plain functions with stage callbacks). Each earlier id is an alias: `get_pipeline_contract(old)` returns the new contract with one `DeprecationWarning` per process; `policy_extract` returns the pipeline for `representation=` when given (else `policy_to_rules`). New `pipeline_for_representation()`. Builder and `run_*` names, the run server's `representation` values and step kinds are unchanged. Where the plan and the code differ: `run_policy_extract` takes no `representation` (the run server picks components by representation over one shared pipeline), so the three policy entries map to representations rather than forwarding a parameter; the `python`, `conditions` and `alignment` representations have no id in the plan and stay reachable by representation only; the `kind: document_ingest` and `kind: investigation_loop` lines in pack manifests are case step kinds, a separate namespace, and are not renamed. Acceptance: each policy id's representation is one the run server builds components for, and those components cover exactly the contract's stages; an earlier id resolves and warns once; the registry, steps-against-builder and table tests pass. Not claimed: a model-backed run of each new id on the Acra corpus (the pipelines are the same function as before).

- **Pipeline registry carries meaning, catalog slice P1 (`pipelines/catalog.py`, `tests/test_pipeline_catalog.py`; +97 / -2 lines, 2 files).** `PipelineContract` gains required `display_name`, `consumes`, `produces` and `output_kind` (`proposals` or `result`), and an `aliases` list (empty until the renames). A display name must read "Input to Output" (a validator and `DISPLAY_NAME_PATTERN`); the six registered pipelines carry theirs: Question to Answer, Documents to Fields, Documents to Vocabulary, Policy to Rules (the `policy_extract` entry, still one entry until the split), Filings to Spread, Case to Decision. New `pipeline_table()` (name, id, in, out, output kind per pipeline) and `pipeline_table_markdown()` for docs and a catalog page. Ids are unchanged. Tests fail on the old registry: every entry states in, out and output kind; a name that does not read "Input to Output" is refused; the table lists every pipeline.

- **A test that the seeded Acra starter is complete (`tests/test_plato_blueprints_api.py`; +25 / -0 lines, 1 file).** On a fresh database, `POST /packs/initialize` then `GET /blueprints/acra-dscr/solution` must list jobs, resolve both members (policy and assistant) and carry no reference. It fails against the seed before the jobs landed ("the starter's solution lists no jobs", checked by pointing the seed root at the earlier tree) and passes now. No change to `plato/seed.py` was needed: `initialize` already publishes the policy pack from the bundled seed packs, the blueprint from the bundled blueprints, and the assistant member from the bundled sample of the same name, so the content landing was the whole fix; the seed-pack vendoring note there stands. A database that already holds policy 0.3.0 published without jobs keeps it (versions are immutable); only a fresh database gets the jobs.

- **An order-dependent test failure fixed at its cause, and a guard against the class (`tests/conftest.py` and eight test files; +62 / -11 lines, 9 files).** `test_config_reports_what_the_replica_actually_resolved` failed whenever `test_plato_settings_store.py` ran before it in one process (`PLATO_DB_BACKEND` read None). Found by bisecting the 66-file selection that reproduced it (also on the 2.6.9 tip): the settings-store tests leave `os.environ` changed (`apply_to_environment` writes it, and tests assign it directly). A probe over the full suite found 18 tests in seven files leaking, and the new guard found 16 more (`test_plato_wiring_default.py` through `build`'s OpenTelemetry defaults, one in `test_otel_tracking.py`). New: an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` fails any test that leaves `os.environ` changed and restores it so the next test is unharmed (pytest's own `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` ignored); a `restored_environment` fixture for tests whose code under test writes the environment, applied to those files; `clean_env` in `test_plato_packs_api.py` now undoes its `monkeypatch` before restoring (a `delenv` after an activation had recorded the activation's value and put it back). The `TODO(settings-store-env-leak)` is resolved. CI shard order: in the current two-shard deal the info-page tests run before the settings-store file, so CI did not hit it; any other pair could have. Verified: the 39 files before the info-page file plus that file pass (they failed), and a deliberate leaking test fails the guard and does not reach the next test. Not mine, failing in the same runs: two `test_formal_canonical_policy` seed tests and two `test_plato_nav_both_ends` tests (another session's uncommitted page edits).

- **Cross-tenant read gap closed in the extraction run store and the turn-run event counter (`server/policy_extract_runs.py`, `policy_extract_runs_db.py`, `policy_extract_api.py`, `pipelines/policy/authoring_chat.py`, `runs/store_db.py`; +203 / -96 lines, 18 files).** The extraction run store read, progressed, updated and finished a run by `run_id` alone, so two tenants holding one run id (possible since the key became tenant-first) read or moved each other's run, and the database `get` would raise on two matches. Now `get`, `heartbeat`, `progress` and `update` take `tenant_id` (keyword, required) and `finish` uses the run's own; both the database and in-process stores key on the pair; the stale sweep stays a deployment-wide job but writes on `(tenant, run, heartbeat)`; `running()` stays a deployment-wide count (a capacity cap). The run routes (`GET runs/{id}`, `/stream`) and the authoring chat's `extraction_status` read through the tenant, so another tenant's run answers 404 or unknown, and two tenants with one id each get their own. The turn-run store numbered events with `max(seq)` over the run id alone, so a second tenant's first event took the first tenant's count; both queries now carry the tenant. **Behavior change** for any caller that passed only a run id to the extraction store or `PolicyExtractionService.get`: it now needs `tenant_id` (a `TypeError` otherwise). Family scan (every select, update, delete and keyed `get` in `jazzx_sdk` and `plato`, by script then by hand): the other Plato-owned stores scope by a tenant helper or key, `get_baseline` and the baselines key on the tenant; what remains unscoped is the seven SDK-only tables with no tenant column (`agent_definition`, `japes_queue_execution`, `conversation_message`, `conversation_overlay`, `materialize_manifest`, `automation_idempotency`, `cost_record`), which wait for the column migration, and the in-process stores, which are per instance. Tests: two tenants with one run id on both stores (memory, sqlite, Postgres) and through the route, a sweep per key, and per-tenant event numbering; they fail on the old signatures and, for event numbering, on the old query.\n\n- **A pre-push step that refuses plan references (scratch `scripts/local`: `check_plan_refs.py` and `test_check_plan_refs.py`, new; `pre_push_check.sh` +11 lines; `commit-msg` +9 lines; not in the japes repository).** Step 2f/4 checks the added lines and commit messages of the pushed range, the same range logic as the spelling check (`--range`, `PUSH_REFS`, `--self-test`, `plan-ref-ok` on a line, `JAPES_SKIP_PLAN_REFS=1`). It fails on the name or path of a gitignored file (`docs/plans`, `docs/status`, `plan_*.md` and the done, stale, note and addendum names, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the file names found in the local plans and status directories) and on the label shapes with zero measured false positives: `K<n>`, `Phase <n>`, `Phase P<n>`, `UAF`, `E<nn>`, "kernel-salvage". It only warns on `item <n>`, `slice <n>`, `step <n> of`, "per the plan", a design document named by role and a bare CHANGELOG. Not checked, because they are real terms here: `P<n>` (policy ids in test data, ARCHITECTURE.md principles), `G<n>` (guideline versions), `§` (named external specs), `plan_*` identifiers. Measured: over the cleaned tree, 0 hard hits and these warn-or-ignored counts (P# 93, G1-5 42, "the plan" 18 mostly the case-plan object, plan_x 95 identifiers, § 58); over the added lines and messages of the last 200 commits, 3 hard hits, all true (the K3 headline of the 2.6.9 squash and two lines of an earlier commit), 0 false. `commit-msg` runs the same hard check on the message and skips it where the script is absent. A test beside the script fails on `job lint gates K3 K4` and passes on the plain form.

- **Plan labels out of tracked text (171 files, +321 / -361 lines).** Comments, docstrings, test docstrings, section dividers and one fixture header no longer point at the gitignored plans. Removed: 84 plan file names and `docs/plans` paths (the `plan_*.md` family and the analysis and design-note names), the `K1` to `K10` kernel-salvage labels (40) and the phrase "kernel-salvage hardening", about 130 `Phase N` and `UAF Phase N` labels, the `P1` to `P8` adjudication and policy labels, `item`/`step` and `the plan's own` phrases, and `Studio design doc`, `chassis doc` and `architecture doc` section references. Each was replaced by the rule in plain words or dropped where the sentence already said it; the KH canonical store's "Phase 1 / Phase 2" became "now / later". Comment-only (`check_comment_only.py`): two exceptions are pydantic `Field` description strings that carried a label (`experts/discovery/schemas.py` `source_timeout`, `fabric/canonical/trace.py` `duration_ms`); the text of those two descriptions changed. Left, as real terms: references to tracked documents (`ARCHITECTURE.md P1` to `P10`), named external specs (`Schema Spec v1.0 §N`, `IIF MSC §7.5`, `Financial Spreading PRD v0.4 §N`, `FR-xxx-N`), guideline set versions (`G1`, `G2`), a policy id `P1` in test data, `F1` score, `noqa` codes, and `§` in a clause-marker regex. Full suite: 12303 passed, 35 skipped, none failed.

- **Tenancy keys, migrations 0037 and 0038 (`plato/migrations/versions/0037_drop_legacy_unique_keys.py`, `0038_tenant_first_in_keys.py`; models `evaluation/datasets_db.py`, `custom_scorers_db.py`, `conductor/suspension_store_db.py`, `server/policy_extract_runs_db.py`; +165 / -8 lines, 8 files).** Option C, first two steps. 0037 drops `uq_eval_dataset_version` and `uq_eval_custom_scorer_revision` (the tenant-leading twins from 0013 stay; no store used the old key, and a lost revision race still raises through the twin). 0038 puts `tenant_id` first in the primary key of `conductor_suspension` and `japes_policy_extraction_run`, the two composite keys with it second and no tenant-leading twin; the composite `get` in the suspension store and its tests take the new order. Each has an up and a down. Verified on sqlite (a key-shape test over every table against its model, a round trip through 0036, rows kept) and on the local Postgres in a scratch schema (up, down, up). Re-run of the table inventory: no other table carries an unscoped multi-column unique key or a non-leading tenant key without a twin. Not built: 0039, 0040, the resolver, the guard flip. Noted, not changed: the extraction-run store reads and updates a run by `run_id` alone, without the tenant.

- **Start 2.7.0 (`pyproject.toml`, `jazzx_sdk/_version.py`, `plato/_version.py`, `jazzx_plato_client/pyproject.toml` and `__init__.py`, `README.md`, `poetry.lock`; +7 / -7 lines, 7 files).** SDK 2.7.0; Plato and the client 0.3.0, as the user chose. Cut from the 2.6.9 tip after the 2.6.9 squash was pushed; the lock's `jazzx-plato-client` entry follows its version. Version, guide and info tests pass.

- **Document processing: folder reading, default input detection, package completeness, digital-PDF tables (+516 / -52 lines, 14 files).**
  `process_dir` reads each file through `process`, so a folder, collection or zip run assesses and reads scanned pages with the
  configured engine exactly as a single file does (it converted first and handed text over, which skipped the per-page engine);
  `process(stage_markdown_to=...)` writes the staged `.md`. `pattern` now defaults to None, meaning every supported type
  (`SUPPORTED_SUFFIXES`), not `*.pdf`; `DocTurn.pattern` likewise. New `pipelines/document/detect.py` `detect_input`: a free,
  model-less detector that refuses a missing, unsupported, empty, unreadable or encrypted file with the reason, routes a PDF to
  `package` on an outline of two or more top-level entries or `DocTurn.package_min_pages` pages (default 20; 0 leaves only the
  outline), else `single`; collection shapes route `collection` (shared `is_collection_turn`). It is opt-in, passed as `detect=`;
  `detect_step`'s default is unchanged. `required_documents` and `completeness_min_confidence` on the document spec, and
  `DocTurn.required` / `min_confidence`, run completeness in `process_package` (new `PackageResult.completeness`, segments count
  by split label and confidence) and `process_dir`; `check_completeness` accepts a `PackageResult`. A digital PDF keeps its ruled
  tables: `SimplePDFProcessor.table_cells` returns DocIntel-shaped cells per page, the conversion's structured view carries them
  (None when no table is found, so a prose PDF is unchanged), and `locate_cell_for_value` lets an extracted value cite
  `PageLocator(page, ref="table N", region="rRcC")`. Tests: folder run with a scanned PDF (fails on the old code), pattern,
  detector, package and directory completeness, table cells and cell locator.

- **Reconcile is one shared module (`pipelines/document/reconcile.py`, `pipelines/steps.py`; +252 / -122 lines, 3 files).** Precedence ranking,
  field filling with conflict resolution (`resolved_by`, `kept`), single-copy conflicts, required-class gaps, precedence validation and the
  per-engine page and cost rows moved out of the case-run document step into `reconcile.py`, which also offers `reconcile_items` (items in,
  record, `filled`, `conflicts` and single-instance conflicts out) for the document pipeline. `steps.py` keeps the same names as thin
  wrappers or re-exports, so callers and the existing tests are unchanged (1406 passed in the case, document, step and precedence suites).
  Tests: who wins a conflict and why, no precedence, agreeing values and submitted values, engine cost rows.

- **Run metrics and a run-to-run diff for documents (`pipelines/document/metrics.py`; +267 / -0 lines, 2 files).** `run_metrics(items)` reduces a
  run (items from a case-run document step, or `items_of` a `DocumentResult`, `PackageResult` or `DirectoryResult`) to
  `DocumentRunMetrics`: per document its class, confidence, taxonomy path, page span in its source file, review pages, admitted field
  values and refused fields; `boundaries` (first page of each cut document, by source file); `page_classes` (class of every page of a
  split file); `refusals`; and `engines` (pages, fallback pages and cost by engine). Documents match across runs on a key of the content
  digest, plus the page span for a cut document. `diff_metrics(before, after)` lists, in a fixed order, documents added or removed,
  moved boundaries, and class, field and refusal changes by document and page; confidence alone is not a difference, so two runs that agree
  give an empty list. Tests cover the shape, stability and each difference kind.

- **Document review: reasons, a pausing step, and attestations that admit a refused field (+240 / -4 lines, 4 files).** New
  `pipelines/document/review.py`: `review_reasons(items, required_fields, conflicts, missing)` lists, in a fixed order, a refused required
  field, a page the split was unsure of, a conflict no precedence decided and a missing required document; `review_gate(reasons_of)` is a
  step that raises `SuspendRun` (key `document_review`) with those reasons and emits an empty `ReviewResolution` when there are none;
  `apply_resolution` admits a resolution's attestations by document. `DocumentAgent.admit_attested(result, attestations)` moves each
  refused field an authorized attestation admits (same `check_action` gate as extraction) into the result's fields, with the refused
  value and where it was read, and no model call; an unauthorized attestation or a refusal without a value stays refused. To make that
  possible a `Refusal` from the document agent now also carries the refused `value` of `doc_type` and a `locator` in `domain_extensions`
  (additive). The recall pass stays inside `process` (it runs when the spec names demanded fields; its reasons are `null_reasons`), so
  there is no separate recall step to build. Tests cover each reason, the pause, an authorized and an unauthorized attestation, and the
  refusal's locator.
- **The document processing pipeline (+343 / -1 lines, 4 files).** New `pipelines/document/process.py`: `build_document_processing_pipeline()`
  (intake, package | collection | single | refuse, reconcile, recall, review, admit, emit, finalize; a `with_` flag drops each optional
  stage), `build_document_processing_components(agent=...)`, `ProcessingTurn` (a `DocTurn` plus `precedence`, `registry`, `submitted` and
  `required_fields`) and `run_document_processing`. Intake uses the default detector (`detect_input`) unless a pack passes its own. Assess,
  read, split, classify, completeness and extract stay inside the agent's process step, each traced as its own span. Reconcile folds every
  document's fields into one record with the winner of each conflict; recall reports what the focused read found and why a demanded
  field is still empty (it runs in the agent); review pauses with typed reasons and resumes with a `ReviewResolution`; admit applies its
  attestations without a model call. A refused input skips every later stage and finalizes as a `Refusal`. `run_document` takes optional
  `step_guards` (default unchanged). Registered as `document_processing` ("Documents to Verified Fields", result). Tests cover the pause
  and resume, a clean run's stages, a refused input and the flags.
- **`documents_to_fields` is the minimal profile of the document processing pipeline (+14 / -2 lines, 2 files).** Both build from the same
  intake, process, emit and finalize step implementations; the registry entry says it is the profile with no reconcile, recall or review,
  and a test pins that its steps are the processing pipeline's with those stages off. `run_document`, `build_document_pipeline` and the
  step ids are unchanged.
- **Locators from the read: a quote-anchored default and a page-aligned mode (+235 / -31 lines, 7 files).** New `locator_mode` on the
  pack spec (`DocumentAgentSpec.locator_mode`, default `DEFAULT_LOCATOR_MODE` = `quote_anchored`), on `DocTurn` (None uses the spec's) and
  as a keyword on `process`, `process_package`, `process_dir` and `extract`, so a pipeline, a pack or one call sets it. `quote_anchored`:
  the quote the extractor already gives in the same call is located in the read (`evidence.quote_span`), and the field's locator is that
  page with a `chars a-b` region; a quote with no certain page, or a pack with quotes off, falls back to the existing value search; no
  extra model call. `page_aligned`: when the read has page regions, `chunk_by_pages` gives one chunk per page and each is extracted on its
  own (`extract_located(page_aligned=True)`), so every field carries the page of the chunk that produced it with no search, at one model
  call per page; a read without page regions is read once. Acceptance is a page plus a character span, not bounding boxes; the
  Document Intelligence element regions are not used. Tests show one call and a page-and-span locator by default, a call per page and a
  page for every field when page-aligned, the one-call fallback without regions, a per-call override, an unknown mode rejected and the
  turn's mode reaching `process`.

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: `explains(text, name=None, amount=None, on=None, large=None, tolerance=0)`, free text that names an item.** True when the text names `name` (whole words in order, as `names` reads them); or states `amount` (magnitude within `tolerance`) AND the date `on` (month/day/year with a two or four digit year, or year-month-day); or, when `large` is stated, states an `amount` of at least `large` written with a "$". An amount alone is False (it can be any other figure in the text); figures are read when they have cents or three or more digits. A cue that is not stated is not used. None when `text` is not stated text, neither `name` nor `amount` is stated, or a stated cue cannot be read (`name` with no word, `amount`, `large` or `tolerance` not a finite number, `tolerance` below zero, `on` not a date). It is the "does this explanation letter name this deposit, debt or payee" test of the codec glue (`letter_explains`), without its table lookup, subject filter and street matching, and with its two inline limits made arguments: the $1 slack is `tolerance` and the 500 "large" is `large`, both stated by the rule (a rule that wants the old behavior passes 1 and 500). Probed with every pair of 24 extreme values across `name`, `amount`, `on`, `large` and `tolerance` against six texts (3,000-digit figures, malformed dates, None); none raises. Tested: 57 cases (name, amount with date, tolerance edges, large with and without "$", date formats, each unreadable cue) and a run in the executor child. Same 1.1.2 and manifest. (+133 / -0 lines, 3 files)

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: `latest(rows, stamp, order=None, ties=False)`, the row with the latest stamp.** From a list of dicts, the row whose `stamp` field (a date, a datetime or ISO text; an offset is converted to UTC, a time without one is taken as written) is latest; a row whose stamp is not stated ranks below every row that states one, `order` names a number field that breaks a tie between equal stamps and ranks the rows when none states a stamp, and a row still tied is won by the one listed last. With `ties=True` it answers the list of every row that shares the winner's stamp (or, with no stamps, its `order`), which is how one run printed twice reads as one run. The answer is the row itself, so a rule reads its other fields. A row that states neither or is not a dict is skipped; None (`[]` with `ties=True`) when no row ranks, and None when `rows` is not a list or `stamp` or `order` is not a field name. It is the "latest AUS run" pick of the codec glue (latest stated run time, else highest paper number, plus every paper stating the same run time), without its AUS tables, paper-name regex or lender clock, which are the pack's. Probed with every pair of 28 extreme stamp and order values (year 1 and 9999 with offsets, 10**400, NaN, sNaN, infinity, bool, bytes, containers; none raises) and a 200,000-row list in 0.12 s. Tested: 25 cases plus 60 extreme combinations, and a run in the executor child. Same 1.1.2 and manifest (the user's 2026-11-02 ruling: the library grows on this version while nothing uses it). (+136 / -1 lines, 3 files)

The count is the matrix list; the script reads `strategy.job-total`. Files, never single tests, are dealt heaviest first to the lightest shard by the seconds per file in the weights file (from one serial run's junit timings; a file it does not list weighs 1 second), so the slow plato API modules and `test_concurrency` are split and module-level state behaves as in a serial run. Each shard has a 25 minute timeout. Locally: shards are disjoint and their union equals the full collection (one parametrize id carries a random uuid, so it differs between collections, nothing else); 162 and 576 files, 3,859 and 8,014 tests, 387 weighted seconds each. Not provable without CI: the real per-shard time (install included), and that a shard never leans on state another file's test leaves. Branch protection: the required check `pytest` keeps its name and now means both shards; shard checks are new names and need not be required. Weights go stale as tests change; regenerate from a junit run. (+864 / -4 lines, 4 files)**

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: the "None when" promises of the new helpers hold at extreme inputs, and so do four older ones (review).** A review found `edate` and `eomonth` raising `OverflowError` for a `months` beyond about 2**31 years (smaller overshoots were caught as `ValueError`) and `round_half_up` raising `decimal.Overflow` for a very negative `places`. Probing every new helper with huge and tiny ints and Decimals, NaN, signaling NaN, infinities, bools, text, mixed and 100,000-item lists found the rest of the family: `_number` compared a signaling NaN (`Decimal("sNaN") != itself` raises), so `at_least`, `at_most`, `within`, `close`, `band`, `ratio`, `percent` and every new helper raised on one; `total` and `average` raised on `[Infinity, -Infinity]` and a Decimal sum past its exponent limit, `average` on two ints too large for a float, and a float sum could answer `inf`; `uncovered_months` (which shares `_anniversary` with `edate`) raised for a `months` of 10**11. Now `_number` asks a Decimal `is_nan()`, a list helper reads an infinity like any other figure it cannot use (the whole answer is None), a sum or mean too large to hold is None, rounding and the date shifts catch `ArithmeticError` with `ValueError`, and `uncovered_months` answers None when the window starts before the dates a date holds. The probe (every pair of 27 extreme values, as value and as places or as list items) found 374 raising calls before and 0 after. The existing `_anniversary` callers `months_between` and `months_between_fraction` take only dates, so their month counts stay in range. Tested: 39 cases (32 fail on the old code: the overflows, the signaling NaN through each helper above, the infinity and too-large lists) and the manifest regenerated for the docstrings that now say "finite" and "too large to hold". (+83 / -27 lines, 3 files)

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: `total`, `average`, `lowest` and `highest`, a list read past its blanks.** Each takes a list or tuple, skips a blank item as `known` reads it (None, `""`, `"n/a"`, `"unknown"`), and answers the sum, mean, smallest or largest of the stated numbers; a float and a Decimal mix as the rest of the library mixes them. Python's `sum` raises on a None among incomes and `max` on a mixed list, so a rule that totals a variable-length list had to filter first. None where `values` is not a list, an item is neither blank nor a number (text such as `"2"`, a bool, NaN: a figure that cannot be read is never skipped), or no item is stated: the total of nothing stated is unknown, not 0, and `total` says to check `gaps` first when a blank must stop the rule. `count` and `any` are not added (`len` and `any` already do those). Tested: 17 cases for `total`, 10 for `average` and 10 for `lowest` and `highest` (blanks of each kind, zero, negatives, Decimal mix, empty, non-list, each unreadable item) and a run in the executor child. Same 1.1.2 and manifest. (+107 / -0 lines, 3 files)

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: `round_half_up`, `round_ceiling` and `round_floor`, Decimal rounding with a stated tie rule.** `round_half_up(value, places=0)` sends a half away from zero (2.5 is 3, -2.5 is -3; Python's `round` sends it to the even neighbor, so 2.5 is 2 and money rounded with it drifts), reading a float as its printed text (1.005 to 2 places is 1.01); `round_ceiling` rounds toward the higher number and `round_floor` toward the lower (named for direction, since "round up" is ambiguous for a negative). All answer a Decimal, `places` is a whole number and may be negative (tens, hundreds), and None where `value` is not a stated number (text, a bool, NaN and infinity are not), `places` is not a whole number or the result is too large for Decimal's precision. Tested: 18 cases for `round_half_up` and 10 each for the other two (ties both signs, float text, negative places, each unstated input) and a run in the executor child. Same 1.1.2 and manifest. (+93 / -1 lines, 3 files)

- **`rules_lib` 1.1.2: `edate(start, months)` and `eomonth(start, months=0)`, a date shifted by whole months.** `edate` keeps the day of the month or falls to that month's last day when it has none (Jan 31 plus 1 is Feb 28, Feb 29 in a leap year); `eomonth` is the last day of the shifted month (the same month by default). Both read a date, a datetime or ISO text as `day` does and answer a `date`; None where `start` is not a date, `months` is not a whole number (a float or a bool is not) or the result falls outside the years a date can hold. They are the date shifts the Income Worksheet formula engine (EDATE, EOMONTH) offers, built on the module's own anniversary rule so the library has one answer for "a month later". Tested: 16 cases for `edate` and 13 for `eomonth` (month ends, leap day, both directions, year rollover, text and datetime input, each unstated input, both ends of the date range) and a run in the executor child. Same 1.1.2 and manifest: nothing uses the library yet, so it keeps growing on this version. (+90 / -0 lines, 3 files)

(+60 / -1 lines, 5 files)** The draft is kept after a publish with its base and open time as they were, so its own version counted as published since it was opened and every later publish from it answered 409 `base_moved`. After a publish under the draft's own pack id, `publish_draft` now moves the draft's base to that version and the time the gate counts from to its `published_at` (`DbPackDraftStore.rebase`, in the `DraftStore` protocol; the draft table has no separate base-time column, so `created_at` carries it and the draft is served with it as `base_at`, see the next entry); a later publish is refused only for a version somebody else published after it, which still names the version. Both tools now build the same text the earlier default gave (its wording plus `Error: <message>`), which `stream_hooks`' tool-error detection still matches. - **A streamed Claude turn reports its usage (`agents/anthropic_native.py`). (+32 / -6 lines, 2 files)** `stream_response` built the completed `Response` with no `usage`, and the Agents runner reads a streamed turn's usage from that event, so a run through the stream counted 0 requests and 0 tokens and any cost read off it was zero. The input counts (cache reads and writes included) arrive in `message_start` and the output count in `message_delta`; the completed response now carries them, through the same `_counts` the blocking path uses. The test reads the completed event's usage and fails on the old code. The live smoke script now counts requests and tokens with a tap on the Anthropic client (independent of the code under test), runs one tool loop per thinking shape (adaptive on claude-haiku-5-5, an enabled budget on claude-haiku-4.5, since the card says haiku-5-5 refuses a budget) with a prompt that needs steps before the tool call, reports per shape whether thinking streamed, whether turn two carried the signed block ahead of the tool call, whether a 400 came back, and cost, and fails when requests or cost read zero after a call returned or when the runner's usage differs from the client's. Worst case 0.1127 USD; the live run passed on 2026-11-01 (adaptive on claude-haiku-5-5 and an enabled budget on claude-haiku-4.5: thinking streamed, the signed block carried on turn two, no 400, the runner's usage equal to the client's; the large call through the stream ok; actual cost 0.003991 USD).

- **The native Claude model takes its output limit from the model card and carries thinking (`agents/anthropic_native.py`; workbench items). (+340 / -16 lines, 2 files)** Limit: `max_tokens` is `model_settings.max_tokens`, else the card's `max_output_tokens` (4096 only for a model with no card). The anthropic client refuses a non-streaming request over about 21,000 output tokens, so `get_response` sends one over `NONSTREAMING_MAX_TOKENS` through the stream and returns the assembled message. Thinking: `model_settings.extra_args["thinking"]` takes `True` or `"adaptive"` (the card's shape), a token budget, or `{type: adaptive|enabled, budget_tokens, display: summarized|omitted}`; `thinking_request` refuses a shape the card says the model rejects (a fixed budget on an adaptive model answers 400) before any call, and the temperature is left out while thinking is on. Streamed thinking is published as `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` events, which `reasoning_delta_text` already reads, and never as answer text; blocking and streamed thinking and redacted-thinking blocks come back as reasoning items (text as the summary, the signature as `encrypted_content`, a redacted block marked by its id), ahead of the answer. `_messages` sends a signed reasoning item back as the thinking block ahead of the assistant turn it precedes, which a tool loop with thinking on requires on its second turn; an unsigned one is still dropped. Tests (mocked stream: thinking, redacted thinking, text, tool use, then the second turn) fail on the old code. Mocks cannot prove the API's own rule, so `scripts/local/smoke_anthropic_thinking.py` runs a two-turn tool loop with streaming and one large non-streaming call live, after printing its worst-case cost (0.0167 USD on claude-haiku-5-5); the live run has not been made.

The API test publishes a version after opening for the 409 and shows the older-line publish passing; the gate test for "already published" now reaches that clause (it failed to before: it passed no base).

A repeat without bound now counts the earlier ones it can consume the same characters as, with nothing between them that forces them to stop (a literal or class none of them can consume ends the run); `MAX_REPEAT_OVERLAP` is 2, which bounds a match to n**3 steps (the extra power is the search's start positions; measured 0.05 s at 500 characters). A repeated body that varies in width and does not begin with a literal nothing else in it can consume is refused, bounded or not (`(a?){30}a{30}`, `(\\w{1,5}){1,40}x`: about 2**30 steps); `(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)+`, the default mnemonic pattern, which the old rule refused although nothing validated it, now passes. `CUE_SENTENCE_CHARS` is 500 (was 2000), the route cue is `\\broute(?:d)?\\b.{0,30}\\bto\\b` (bounded, was three words), and the guide topic pattern's date gap is `\\s{0,3}`. - **An authored pattern that could pin a worker is refused where it is declared (`safety/patterns.py`; found in review of the profile editor, which lets an author write `reference_cues` that the lint runs over every job's text).** Python's `re` has no timeout, and no safer engine (`re2`, `regex`) is a dependency, so `check_pattern` holds a pattern to a subset by reading its parsed form, never running it: at most `MAX_PATTERN_CHARS` (200) long, compiling, no backreference, no repeat of more than `MAX_NESTED_REPEAT` (5) turns over a body that repeats without bound or branches (the exponential shapes `(a+)+`, `(a*)*`, `(a|aa)+`, `(\w+\s?)+`, `(.*a){12}`, `(x+x+)+y`), no bounded repeat over `MAX_REPEAT_BOUND` (1000), at most `MAX_WIDE_REPEATS` (2) unbounded wildcards (`.*`, a negated class, `\w+`; adjacent ones cost the input's length to that power) and `MAX_UNBOUNDED_REPEATS` (10) unbounded repeats, and a list holds at most `MAX_PATTERNS_PER_LIST` (50). It is a conservative subset, not a proof: what passes is polynomial of low degree, so the text it runs over is bounded too (`CUE_SENTENCE_CHARS` 2,000 for a cue, `MAX_HEADING_CHARS` 500 for a guide heading). Applied to every pattern an author or a caller declares that a server then runs: `ReferenceCues` (all four lists), `lint_filters.yaml`'s `detail_matches`, `MnemonicRules.pattern`, and `MarkdownGuide` and `SectionPathHeader` patterns (so a guide profile accepted by a route is held to it). Every default the SDK ships passes; a refusal is an `UnsafePattern` (an `AuthoredValueError`), surfaced by pydantic as a `ValidationError` where a model holds the pattern, so the profile editor's route no longer needs its own compile. Not verified: patterns in `tools/documents/chunking.py` and `classify.py` (called with strings from code and config, not found reaching a route; not checked further). Tests: ten catastrophic shapes refused without being run, ordinary and default patterns pass, length, count, backreference, wildcard and bound refusals, every cue class, the lint filter, guide and mnemonic patterns, and a long line cut before matching. - **A run that died before its first step is retried, and a run the user stopped then orphaned ends stopped (`runs/`; workbench rank 5).** `reap_stale` failed every stale RUNNING run, whether or not it had begun and whether or not the user had asked it to stop. `TurnRun` gains `attempts` (claims made; a handed-back claim is not counted), `max_attempts` (None, the default, keeps today's behavior), `not_before` and `started_at` (set when the first event is journaled, so a run that may already have acted is never retried). `reap_update` decides for both stores: a stale run with `stop_requested` ends INTERRUPTED with its stop reason and no error; one with no `started_at` and attempts left goes back to QUEUED, its claim cleared, after a backoff (`RETRY_BASE_SECONDS` 5, doubling to `RETRY_MAX_SECONDS` 300); any other is FAILED as before. `claim_next` and `claim_any` skip a run still inside its backoff (its key waits, FIFO), in the in-process and the `fabric.db` store. - **A draft whose base version has moved on cannot publish, and a file holding a merge conflict cannot publish (`pack/publish_gate.py`, `pack/check.py`, `plato/api/packs.py`; workbench rank 4, the merge itself stays deferred).** A draft records the version it was opened from, but nothing compared it to the pack's newest version, so a publish stood over a newer one on edits made against an older base. `refuse_moved_base` raises `BaseMoved` (naming both versions) when a draft opened from a version finds a different one newest; the draft publish route answers 409 `{"code": "base_moved", "base_version", "latest_version"}`. A draft with no base (created fresh, from a sample or by an import) is not held to one, and a `pack_version` already published still gets the store's immutability refusal. `conflict_marker_files` finds a start line, a separator and an end line in order (a setext heading underlined with `=======` is not one), and `check_pack_archive` reports it as the publish-blocking finding `conflict_markers`, so an upload is held to it too. - **`session_advisory_lock`: one holder per key across commits (`fabric/db/locking.py`; workbench rank 3).** The SDK had only `advisory_xact_lock` and its try form, which end with the transaction, so a section that commits partway is no longer guarded, and `concurrency/guard.py` is Redis and fails open. `session_advisory_lock(engine, key, wait_seconds=0, poll_seconds=DEFAULT_POLL_SECONDS)` takes `pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtext(key))` on a connection of its own (AUTOCOMMIT), raises `SessionBusyError` when the key is not free (at once, or after polling to the deadline), and releases when the block ends however it ends: a failed unlock invalidates the connection (ending the session, so a pooled connection cannot carry the lock to its next user) and the release is shielded so a cancelled holder still frees the key. The same `hashtext` key space as the transaction helpers. A no-op on sqlite. Not verified: a pooler in transaction mode (it cannot hold a session lock), the interaction with `session_guard` and `shield` (the lock holds no session). Tests: refused while held and admitted after, a commit inside the block does not release, a waiter gets it within its wait, a wait that runs out raises, a cancelled holder releases, different keys are independent; the Postgres cases run against the local Postgres and skip on sqlite. - **A metric key several jobs write is an error only when they compute it differently under different names (`jtbdset_lint.py`; raised by jaci's Pulte export gate).** `metric-key-owned-twice` was an error for any second writer, which the vendored workbench check meant as one writer per key and which has no notion of a job that defines a metric and others that read it; an imported catalog has no field to say so. A profile's `severity` map takes the new code. - **An ontology source: a catalog that says where it came from, refreshed from the Knowledge Hub without failing a caller (`pack/ontology_source.py`; plan `plan_ontology_source`).** `OntologySource.refresh(kh)` fetches the Hub ontology named by Hub id or registry key, unwraps it from the Hub's envelope (`json_ontology` and eight other keys, a JSON string, or a bare schema), refuses one that looks corrupt (not an object, no entity map, under `min_entities` (5), no entity with properties, a required entity missing), and adopts the rest; it never raises (`adopted`, `unchanged`, `rejected` with the reason, `unavailable`), the TTL clock runs after a failure too, and `current()` is the local read, the bundled seed until something is adopted. `OntologyStamp` is the provenance under a catalog's `x-provenance`: the keys a pack carries today (`source_file`, `source_id`, `source_version`, `source_sha256`, `scope`, `entities_read`) plus a typed `source_status` (`seed` or `hub`), `fetched_at`, `hub_id` and `hub_version`; a stamp with only the free-text `status` reads as a seed, so an existing seed pack loads unchanged, and `confirmed` means fetched from the Hub with the digest recorded. A pack declares the Hub ontology in a `catalog_source:` manifest block (`PackManifestLoader.catalog_source_config`). `stamped_catalog` is what a new pack version publishes when a seed upgrades to a Hub-sourced catalog. True for an IP literal in a private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast or unspecified range (the ranges `is_private_ip` refuses) or a name the caller lists (case-insensitive); any other name passes. Tests fail the run if the check touches a resolver. (+17 / -1 lines, 1 file; +39 lines, 1 test file)

Two differences are pinned as the contract: a graph read wraps a transport failure in `KnowledgeFabricError` where the raw call raises it as is, and `docs.get` is not a drop-in for `get_document`: it raises on a missing document (the raw call answers `None`) and follows the retrieval mode, so a LOCAL fabric never asks the hub. A host that wants the raw behavior keeps `fabric.kh.get_document`. (+105 lines, 1 test file)

Test: a template section cut three ways files its jobs under it with its own prefix and no derived-prefix note. (+41 / -5 lines, 4 files)

The other callers of `build_invocation_context_from_headers` already map it. Test: a non-UUID claim is refused with a 400 naming it, a valid one is admitted. (+29 / -1 lines, 2 files)

The attribute is now a read property with the same one-time warning. Test: the read warns and returns the scope. (+25 / -0 lines, 2 files)

(+14 / -12 lines, 3 files)
- **What a rerun does when nothing changed is a setting: `rerun.when_unchanged`.** `continue` (the default, and what a rerun did before) copies the followed run's verdicts and finishes the conductor over them; `stop_copy` ends the run `complete` at once with those outcomes; `stop_empty` ends it `complete` with none (`stop_reason: no_impacted_rules`, the caller reads the followed run). Both stops end through `ConductorState.finish`, so no later step runs: no investigation, governor, human approval or narrative. **`stop_copy` after an approved decision therefore skips re-approval; the pack author sets it in `pack_manifest.yaml` (`rerun: {when_unchanged: ...}`, `PackManifestLoader.rerun_config`) and a submitter may override it in the `rerun` body (`RerunSpec.when_unchanged`, the client's `RerunRequest`); submit beats pack beats `continue` (`when_unchanged_of`).** Nothing-changed is computed from the inputs alone, so a rule that reads the date can have another answer today with no input change; the stops keep the old answer and skip the steps that might have caught it (also stated on the option). It is decided where the pack adjudicates, so a pack with no adjudication step ignores it. An unknown value is refused at submit (422) and by lint (`unknown_rerun_when_unchanged`). Tests (stop and empty fail on the old code): each value, a changed rerun ignoring it, a stopped run persisted, precedence, refusal, lint, the run input carrying the resolved value. Not covered end to end: a pack-declared value through the service. (+218 / -7 lines, 9 files)
- **A step can end a run complete: `ConductorState.finish`.** `state.halt` stops a run and reports it `halted`, which is a failure to a caller; there was no way for a step that had nothing left to do to stop the rest. A component that sets `state.finish = True` ends the run `complete`: the steps after it (and, inside a loop, the rest of the loop and the steps after it) do not run, and the step itself is recorded `ran`. `halt` and `stopped` are unchanged. The bundle leaves the file out and says so (and that the workbook is built without it), `CoverageDelta` carries `ledger_error_before` and `ledger_error_after`, and the solution view's coverage block carries `ledger_error`. The draft coverage route already returned the field; the modes and diagnosis stay tolerant, and the lint names the file. (+22 / -5 lines, 5 files)

(+14 / -2 lines, 4 files)

It refuses with the pack's `document_registry_error`, as the draft route does. (+3 / -0 lines, 2 files)

An adopted entry's aliases join the names a later entry of the same request is matched against, so one named like an earlier alias is listed as present instead of becoming a second type. - **Guidance assets have a durable, tenant-scoped store.** `DbGuidanceStore` (`jazzx_sdk.fabric.guidance.db_store`,

  that read taken out of the step's loop, which now calls it too: the pack's taxonomy, schema and engine classify,
  split when asked and extract, and it returns the items, the usage by mode, the step's settings and the step used

- **Stored documents are indexed, and listed by subject or label.** The blob store keeps a document by its digest and
  could not be listed, so a caller held every id. A table `document_record` (migration 0034, `DbDocumentIndex`)

  (a connection that failed before it was sent, 429, 503), always with the one `Idempotency-Key` and trace id the call

- **An assessment chooses which engine decides a requirement that has a job and its code.** `assess(engine_mode=,
  primary=)`, the `policy_assessment` step's `engine_mode:` and `primary:`, and an eval experiment's `config`
  take one of five modes (`jazzx_sdk.pack.engine_modes`). **`hybrid` is the new default**: each job's code runs
  first; a violation stands and the job is skipped; a satisfied verdict stands when the code covers the whole
  job (every check computable, the coverage report's `code` disposition), otherwise the job still runs for its
  other checks; code that cannot decide (missing data, an unreadable fact, an executor error, a gate that does
  not hold) sends the job to the model, and without an executor every job runs. `all` is the earlier behaviour,
  every rule on its own, which counted a requirement twice when a job and its code both failed. `code_only` runs
  the rules that are not procedures and lists the jobs with no code as `not_covered`; `jobs_only` runs the
  procedures; `both` runs code and job apart for each pair, returns the two verdicts side by side

## [2.6.3] - unreleased

- **Model pricing re-verified on 2026-10-16.** `scripts/update_model_pricing.py` found no price changes: the
  anthropic, openai, gemini and Azure Document Intelligence `verified` dates move to 2026-10-16, and
  `gemini-3-flash-preview` is marked `deprecated`. (+6 / -5 lines, 1 file)
- **Plato closes its grounding sessions at shutdown.** A replica that stopped with a session open left that
  session's directory (`session-<key>-...`) behind in the temp directory, or in `PLATO_GROUND_DIR`; the app's
  lifespan now drains the grounding registry, which closes each session and removes its directory
  (`GroundingSessions.drain`). The grounded-assistant test points `PLATO_GROUND_DIR` at its own temporary
  directory and asserts it is empty once the app is down (+28 / -2 lines, 5 files).

- **`mcp` floor `>=1.30.0` and `Mako` 1.4.3 in the lock (Dependabot).** The MCP Streamable HTTP session accumulation
  alert is fixed from 1.30.0 and 2.2.0; the lock resolves `mcp` to 2.3.0 (no ceiling, `jazzx_sdk/mcp/compat.py`
  covers both majors), which drops `httpx-sse` and adds `mcp-types`. Mako's drive-letter path traversal is fixed from
  1.4.2 (transitive, lock only). The MCP tests pass on 1.28.1 and 2.3.0 (43); the transport-security test read
  `_session_manager`, which 2.x names `session_manager`, and now reads either. (+41 / -40 lines, 4 files)

- **`KernelClient` takes SDK types for an agent invocation, and can start one or stream it.** A consumer no longer
  imports `kernel_client.models`: `invoke_agent` (signature kept) gains `messages` (user, assistant and tool-result
  turns as `AgentMessage`s or `{"role", "text"}` mappings, in place of `input_text`), `overrides`
  (`AgentOverrides`: prompt, model, temperature, reasoning effort, verbosity, steps, feedback, output schema, tools,
  callable agents, MCP servers), `hooks` (`AgentHook`, an `on_complete` webhook), `streaming`
  (`StreamingConfig`), `parent_notepad_id` and `project_id` (sent as `x-request-project-id`). `start_agent` returns
  the invocation id without polling; `stream_agent` starts with streaming on and yields the invocation stream's
  events (dicts) until `done` or `error`, reading from the start so none published before the first read is lost
  (the caller gives the `RedisStreamClient`). The types live in `jazzx_sdk.clients.kernel_invoke` (re-exported from
  `jazzx_sdk.clients`), which writes the request JSON itself and maps the same inputs onto the generated request;
  tests hold the two equal and compare the generated overrides, webhook and enum fields with the SDK's, so a
  client upgrade that renames one fails there. `session_id` stays a documented no-op. File and tool-call-request
  message content are not modelled. A kernel 422 on `start_agent` raises (it was returned as the invocation id); a
  tool-result message needs its `tool_call_id` and no other message may carry one; an empty `messages` list is
  refused like a missing one, and `input_text` with any `messages` is refused, by the client and the mock alike
  (the mock also needs `stream_client`); a mapping's `content` is read when its `text` is `None`; mapping content is read as text or text parts and a file part is
  refused. `MockKernelClient` follows the same call rules and gains `start_agent` and `stream_agent` (+710 / -59
  lines, 6 files).

- **Folding keeps a distinct requirement and what a folded job knew.** Four review fixes to the fold. A single-digit
  figure now counts when two jobs are compared (`figures(text, single_digits=True)`, used by the fold only: "at least
  2 open tradelines" no longer folds with "at least 3"); the helper's default still leaves single digits out for the
  alignment and ledger matching that share it. A survivor that had no reads and gains some from a folded job is
  marked not assessed (`computable_checks` None) rather than "none computable". Two jobs of one section never end up
  folded together through a job of another section: the blocked link is listed as a possible duplicate. A folded
  job's data mapping (`mapped_reads`), its undeclared documents and the entity types and metrics (by metric key) the
  survivor lacks are carried onto it beside its reads (a carried metric is renumbered under the survivor's own
  stem, so mnemonics stay unique); its filing (source, section type, assistant, mnemonic, kind) stays the
  survivor's. The entity and metric metadata keys are constants beside the writer (+208 / -8 lines, 4 files).

- **`KernelClient` works without a token.** `token` is optional: with one it builds `kernel_client.AuthenticatedClient`
  as before, with none (`None` or empty) it builds `kernel_client.Client` and sends no `Authorization` header,
  the way `KnowledgeHubClient` does; the request-headers hook and pool limits are unchanged. `ClientLayer.kernel`
  passes its bearer token through as is, so an unauthenticated caller no longer sends `Authorization: Bearer `
  with an empty value. `MockKernelClient` already takes an optional token and the process-client block is
  commented out, so neither changed (+56 / -10 lines, 3 files).

  (domain pack, surface binding, client overlay, execution profile) with its member, artifact and a summary
